questions.q: What two arguments does the azurerm_resource_group resource require?
options: subscription_id and tenant_id
resource_group_name and virtual_network_name
address_space and location
name and location
questions.explain: azurerm_resource_group only needs a name and a location — no address space or networking arguments belong on it.

questions.q: Why is azurerm_virtual_network's address_space argument written as a list, e.g. ["10.0.0.0/16"], even when it holds a single CIDR block?
options: Because address_space is actually optional and the brackets are decorative
Because a VNet can technically be assigned more than one address range, so the schema is a list
Because Terraform requires every argument to be a list regardless of type
Because azurerm_subnet shares the same variable with the VNet
questions.explain: A VNet's address space is modeled as a list because Azure allows a VNet to have more than one CIDR range, even though most VNets use just one.

questions.q: In azurerm_subnet, what does the virtual_network_name argument reference?
options: The parent VNet's name, as a string — not a generated resource ID
A numeric subnet index
The resource group's location
The subscription's tenant ID
questions.explain: azurerm_subnet attaches to its VNet by name string, via virtual_network_name — a different reference style from the generated-ID pattern AWS uses for subnets.

questions.q: Why does Terraform create azurerm_resource_group.example before azurerm_virtual_network.example in this lesson's configuration, even though no depends_on is written anywhere?
options: Because Terraform alphabetizes resource types before planning
Because azurerm_resource_group is a special resource type that always runs first
Because the VNet block references azurerm_resource_group.example.location and .name, so Terraform infers the dependency automatically
Because resource blocks are always created in the order they're typed in the file
questions.explain: Terraform's dependency graph is built from attribute references. The VNet can't know the resource group's location until that resource group exists, so Terraform schedules it first — no explicit depends_on needed.

questions.q: In the lesson's terraform plan output, "Plan: 4 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy" refers to which four resources?
options: Two virtual networks and two resource groups
Four separate resource groups
The resource group, the virtual network, and the two subnets
The resource group, the virtual network, and two network interfaces
questions.explain: The configuration declares exactly four resources — azurerm_resource_group.example, azurerm_virtual_network.example, azurerm_subnet.web, and azurerm_subnet.app — all marked for creation.
